title: tenant data-locality enforcer + KMS-usage audit proxy
author: Nora Patel
description:
Summary: Introduces a runtime policy enforcer that ensures tenant data locality constraints (region pinning) are enforced at request admission time and a lightweight KMS-usage audit proxy that records KMS operation metadata for compliance pipelines. This PR implements an attribute-driven RBAC v2 hook to validate tenant claims against geography policies, adds audit enrichment for KMS calls, and wires a feature-flagged rollout for Private and Dedicated clusters.

Motivation and context: Customers in regulated industries require both preventive controls (reject requests that would use keys outside allowed regions) and deterministic audit trails of encryption operations. Previous mitigations were post-hoc—alerts and reconciliations—which do not provide safe-fail guarantees. This work closes the loop by failing the request pre-execution when tenant policy and key location mismatches occur, while also emitting an immutable audit envelope for downstream compliance ingestion. Related Linear: ENG-3842 (data locality enforcer), SEC-1120 (kms audit pipeline). Linked Support ticket: SUP-2147.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/policy: new tenant_locality_enforcer module (admission hook) implementing attribute-based checks against tenant configuration
- auth/rbac: extended RBAC v2 attribute mapping to include tenant_geo and allowed_key_zones; added unit tests for attribute evaluation
- kms/proxy: added kms_audit_proxy sidecar that intercepts KMS calls from the runtime, annotates with request and tenant metadata, and forwards to configured KMS endpoint (no key material changes)
- observability: metrics (policy.rejects, policy.evaluations_total, kms.audit_events) and tracing spans for end-to-end correlation
- config: new feature flag features.enforce_tenant_locality and migration script to populate default tenant geographic claims
- docs: drafted compliance runbook and operator notes for rollout and troubleshooting

Commits (summary):
- a1b2c3d: initial tenant_locality_enforcer scaffold and interface definitions
- d4e5f6a: attribute evaluation engine + test cases for edge conditions (multi-zone tenants, fallback keys)
- b7c8d9e: kms_audit_proxy implementation + protobuf/transport contract
- f0e1d2c: metrics and tracing hooks + dashboards json
- 0a1b2c3: integration tests and migration tool for tenant claims
- final: squash & polish, add operator docs

Files changed (representative):
- runtime/policy/tenant_locality_enforcer.go (new)
- auth/rbac/v2/attribute_mapper.go (modified)
- kms/proxy/audit_proxy.go (new)
- tools/migrations/2026-01-tenant-geo-claims.sql (new)
- observability/dashboards/policy-enforcer.json (new)
- docs/operators/data-locality-runbook.md (new)

Behavioural notes and compatibility:
- Default behaviour is opt-in via features.enforce_tenant_locality=false. When enabled, the enforcer returns HTTP 403 with a well-structured error payload that includes policy_violation details and suggested remediation (e.g., use tenant-scoped key or request allowlist).
- KMS audit proxy is transparent to key operations (it does not manage keys); it signs events and emits them to the audit log stream. Customers running Private may opt to route audit events to their on-prem compliance collector.
- RBAC v2 attribute changes are additive; existing roles continue to function. We add a migration that synthesizes tenant_geo claims from existing tenant metadata if not present.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Julian Park (reviewer): "Nice separation of concerns. I want to see stronger unit tests around multi-region tenants and a failure mode where the KMS endpoint is unreachable. Also request that the audit payload avoids logging PII (tenant id and request id only)."
- Nora (author): "Added tests for multi-region and network failure behaviour; audit payload redaction implemented (PII scrubber). See commit d4e5f6a and kms proxy change for redaction."
- Aisha Rahman (reviewer): "How does this interact with existing autoscaling and request routing? If we reject because of key region mismatch, will clients see consistent latencies?"
- Nora: "Added tracing spans and a fast-path check before heavy scheduling logic so latency delta is <1ms in the common pass case. Included micro-benchmark numbers in the PR comments."
- Marco Gutierrez (security): "Recommend adding a brief e2e that demonstrates audit events landing in Splunk; otherwise LGTM."
- Nora: "Added Splunk integration smoke test and included it in the CI matrix behind a nightly job tag."

CI and test summary: all unit and integration tests pass; static analysis and license checks pass. A nightly-only Splunk smoke test runs as expected. Benchmarks: enforcer fast-path adds ~0.7ms median to a 50ms median request; cold-path (policy mismatch) returns immediately with a 403.

Rollout plan and operator notes:
1) Deploy kms_audit_proxy as an opt-in sidecar in Dedicated and Private clusters.
2) Enable features.enforce_tenant_locality=false and run migration to seed tenant_geo claims.
3) Run for 2 weeks in audit-only mode (enforcer logs but does not reject), monitor policy.evaluations_total and policy.rejects.
4) Flip features.enforce_tenant_locality=true for a subset of tenants (canary group) and monitor errors and support tickets.
5) Full rollout with a staged increase and operator runbook in docs/operators/data-locality-runbook.md.

Release notes:
- Add: Tenant Data Locality Enforcer (feature-flagged).
- Add: KMS Audit Proxy for recording KMS operation metadata.
- Add: RBAC v2 attribute mapping for tenant_geo and allowed_key_zones.

Security / compliance impact: This PR reduces the risk surface by preventing cross-region key usage that would violate residency constraints and provides deterministic audit telemetry for KMS operations. No key material leaves the KMS; the proxy only annotates and forwards operations.

Follow-ups and known limitations:
- Need to formalize audit event retention and signing policy with legal/compliance (ticket SEC-1158).
- The migration synthesizes tenant_geo claims from best-effort metadata—operators should verify for accuracy before enforcement.
- Additional work planned to integrate with policy-as-code tooling for central governance (ENG-3901).

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals from Julian, Aisha, and Marco. All CI checks green at merge time.
